implemented_scope: Bounded local first-order sensitivity and covariance; known source identities; explicit rejection of unsupported nonlinear propagation. No claim of complete GUM conformity.

sources.title: JCGM 100:2008 — Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement
sources.short_excerpt: should not be given with an excessive number of digits
sources.implementation_note: Covariance with signed local sensitivities; reporting generally at most two significant uncertainty digits, nominal at matching place, unrounded internal values retained. Two digits are the chosen display default, not a universal laboratory requirement.

sources.title: JCGM 100:2008/Amd.1:2026 — Nonlinearity in measurement models
sources.short_excerpt: When the nonlinearity of f is significant
sources.implementation_note: Significant nonlinear terms can affect both central estimate and uncertainty. Higher-order propagation or Monte Carlo is outside NumOS production scope; unreliable first-order cases return an explicit status. The original mathematical nominal is not asserted to be the corrected output expectation.

sources.title: JCGM GUM-6:2020 — Developing and using measurement models
sources.short_excerpt: A simpler but less rigorous way
sources.implementation_note: Annex F compares local model and linearization at each input plus/minus its standard uncertainty. This is not a proof for arbitrary functions. NumOS curvature thresholds and a three-u domain neighbourhood are conservative product choices, not JCGM numerical mandates.

sources.title: JCGM 101:2008 — Propagation of distributions using a Monte Carlo method
sources.short_excerpt: linearization of the model provides an inadequate representation
sources.implementation_note: Monte Carlo is a consulted alternative for nonlinear distribution propagation, not implemented in production. NumOS user measurement input does not assign a distribution.

sources.title: NIST Technical Note 1297 — Reporting uncertainty
sources.short_excerpt: Report U together with the coverage factor k used to obtain it
sources.implementation_note: Report standard u or expanded U with k. NumOS chooses k=2 for the expanded display; no automatic 95 percent confidence statement is justified without distribution and degrees-of-freedom information.
